content.rationale:
The release is one program, scripts/release.js, and it takes the version only as an explicit argument. It reads the first non-flag argument or --version <value> / --version=<value>, treats the two spellings as the same thing, and refuses everything else: no argument, use of any other flag, or a value that is not a major.minor.patch triple (prerelease and build suffixes allowed) exits non-zero after printing a usage line that names the version, before anything is read for packing. There is no default, no fallback to the manifest's committed 0.0.1, no derivation from a tag, date or counter, and no second source of any kind, so a value that reaches an artifact has come from the argument and from nowhere else (sppkuruw).

The stamping is ephemeral by construction rather than by restore. The tree's package.json is read once, parsed, and copied; the copy's version field is set to the argument and the copy is serialised into the archive as extension/package.json. The file on disk is never opened for writing, so there is nothing to restore, nothing to leave behind and no window in which the stamped value exists in the tree. The same reasoning rules out the two other ways a release could commit the value: nothing is installed or resolved, so no lockfile is written, and nothing is built, so no generated file is written. The run's only write to the tree is the artifact itself, once, at the end, from a buffer assembled in memory — the archive is not staged through a temporary file, and no backup of the manifest is made. After the run the tree is byte-for-byte the tree it found, apart from the .vsix.

The artifact is assembled offline with the zip writer in the same file: node:zlib deflate, local headers, a central directory and its end record, built whole in memory and written once. Shelling out to vsce was not an option and is not a loss: its prepublish hook runs npm run build, esbuild is a dev dependency that a release tree need not have installed, and an install step is exactly what writes the lockfile that would carry the value. Writing the zip directly keeps the release a single file with no packager, no network, no build and no dependency, which is also why the entry point needs no helper module and no package script (package.json is srlrwowp's, and it is untouched).

What is packaged is vqultolm's set and nothing else: out/extension.js, media/webview.html, src/webview/main.js, every src/styles/*.css, @vscode/codicons/dist/codicon.css with the codicon.ttf it loads (with its font path preserved, since the stylesheet resolves it relatively), the manifest, and the tree's README when it has one — each under the extension/ directory the format puts the packaged extension in. A file of that set the tree does not carry is reported and left out rather than fabricated: a tree without the gitignored build outputs or without node_modules packages what it holds, instead of building, installing or inventing the rest, and fabricating them is the only way it could change the tree. Two further entries sit at the archive root and not under extension/: extension.vsixmanifest (whose Identity carries the same release value, as the vsix format has the identity mirror the manifest) and [Content_Types].xml, the container's description of the archive. Those two describe the archive rather than the extension, and they are what makes the output a vsix a host installs rather than a bare zip; extension/ itself holds exactly the set vqultolm records, so no other file of the extension ships.

The artifact is named <name>-<version>.vsix, the packager's own convention, and is written into the root of the tree it runs in — where the repository's ignore rules already anticipate a .vsix. Nothing else about it is fixed here: the flag spelling, the filename and the packager are the release's own choices, and the value's shape is only narrowed to what a host will install.
